clue.text: Master part of 24, for example

definitions.meaning: old British slang for a schoolmaster (or a magistrate)
24 is DUCK (from 26/24, DAFFY DUCK), and a duck's bill is one example of a bird's part of this name

explanation.surface: A teacher seems to be described as one component of some other numbered thing.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' points to 24-down, the second half of DAFFY DUCK, so the second definition is a part of a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: British school slang calls a teacher this, and a bird's hard mouth is named the same way.

clue.text: Little Mexican legend with zip, so easy to miss one whizzing about

indicators.note: letters whizzing about are thrown into a new order, the anagram signal
to miss a letter is to leave it out of the word before it

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A tiny Mexican hero is so quick that he is hard to catch as he zooms around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to miss one' drops I from ZIP, leaving ZP; 'whizzing about' then shuffles LEGEND, ZP, SO and EASY together.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon mouse billed as the fastest in all Mexico is a small Looney Tunes character.

clue.text: Owners of smart rabbit warren tidied up burrows regularly (also half a dozen others here)

indicators.note: tidying something up rearranges its parts, so the letters of warren are put in a new order
regularly means taking every other letter of burrows

explanation.surface: A clever rabbit's keepers tidy its warren and its burrows; the aside hints the studio owns several more of the grid's stars.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed aside is extra information: the studio also owns the six other characters entered in this grid (Speedy, Sam, Elmer, Pepe, Daffy, Tweety).
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollywood studio owns Bugs Bunny, the wisecracking cartoon rabbit, as part of its Looney Tunes stable.

clue.text: 24's tale

parts.note: 24 is DUCK; the French word for a duck is also an English word for a false story, so a duck's tale

explanation.surface: A short reference to a story belonging to the duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is 24-down, DUCK. The answer is French for duck and, in English, a hoax or false report: the duck's own word is a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: In English the borrowed word means an unfounded rumour or hoax story, while in French it simply names the waterfowl.

clue.text: Hole inverted, nothing in squash bottle

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word for squash

parts.note: jam means a squash or crush, as in a traffic jam

indicators.note: inverted means turned upside down, so in a down clue the word for hole is read backwards

parts.note: a bore is a hole drilled out, as in a borehole
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Instructions for an odd drink: a hole turned over, nothing, then squash in a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inverted' turns BORE into EROB; with O it goes 'in' JAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeroboam is a very large wine or champagne bottle, holding several ordinary bottles' worth.

clue.text: See 16
Gunslinger certainly before noon holding old competitor of ours up

indicators.note: holding means the word for certainly wraps round the next piece

parts.note: yes means certainly, as an emphatic reply

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the piece is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the Times is a rival newspaper of the Guardian, where this puzzle appears
AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: A cowboy says yes before midday while clutching an old rival newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ours' is the Guardian speaking, so its rival is a newspaper; 'up' reverses that paper plus O to OSEMIT, and 'holding' wraps the word for certainly round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-moustached Looney Tunes outlaw is a pistol-toting gunfighter of the cartoon Wild West.

clue.text: Natural opener not opening with the others

indicators.note: not opening means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a petal is something in nature that opens out as the flower blooms

explanation.surface: A batsman who opens naturally fails to open the innings with his teammates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not opening' removes the first letter, P.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation et alii stands for 'and others', used after a first name in a list.

clue.text: Walk where mountains crossed by East European to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue going to the west means reading from right to left, backwards
the mountains are crossed by the traveller, who goes round them on both sides here

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark
the Alps are the obvious mountains

explanation.surface: A walking route where an easterly European traveller crosses the mountains heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossed by' gives EDANALPSE, the mountains sitting within the traveller, and 'to the west' reverses the lot, as across clues read west to east.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafront promenade is a broad, level path for strolling along.

clue.text: Vessel restricted, contrarily packed with oxygen

indicators.note: packed with means the next piece is stuffed inside
contrarily means the other way round, so the word for restricted is read backwards

parts.note: tabu, a variant spelling of taboo, means forbidden or restricted
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A ship whose supply is limited, but which is still packed with oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrarily' turns TABU into UBAT; 'packed with' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat is a German submarine, a seagoing craft.

clue.text: Leather making a comeback with chic designer

indicators.note: making a comeback means going back the way it came, so the word for leather is read backwards

parts.note: elk is leather made from the hide of the elk
in means fashionable, chic

explanation.surface: Leather goods return to fashion along with a stylish fashion house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' turns ELK into KLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvin Klein is the American fashion designer whose name is a clothing label.

clue.text: Very much in the past, occasional ale drunk

parts.note: ago means in the past
odd means occasional, as in the odd drink

indicators.note: drunk means the letters of ale are mixed up, as if tipsy

explanation.surface: Someone once drank the odd ale, but very much of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' shuffles ALE into EAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a great amount or to a large extent.

clue.text: Degenerate leader on tour of constituency's ending in a number of beds?

indicators.note: a leader on a tour of a place goes round it, so the shuffled leader goes round the letter
degenerate means to fall into ruin, so the letters of leader are broken up and rearranged
ending means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A corrupt politician tours the constituency, perhaps sleeping in many beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degenerate' turns LEADER into LAERED, which goes round Y, the last letter of 'constituency's'. Beds here are geological strata, not places to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock or soil laid down in strata is arranged in layers, each a distinct bed.

clue.text: See 25
Edge on high in wrong position

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the word for edge comes after the word for high

parts.note: high means off, as in food that has gone bad
a side is an edge of something

explanation.surface: A climber's ledge high up is the wrong spot to stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' is rotten food, not tall: meat that is high has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: In football and rugby a player in an illegal position ahead of the ball is offside.

clue.text: Supporting offers made hostile

parts.note: for means in favour of, supporting
bidding is the making of offers at an auction

explanation.surface: Backing for offers became unfriendly.
explanation.definitionFit: A forbidding manner or landscape is unfriendly and threatening, so it is hostile.

clue.text: Hunter: feud with me and devious leporine rival originally animated

indicators.note: animated means set in lively motion, so the letters are mixed
originally means taking the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A hunter's feud with me and a cunning rabbit-like rival, first drawn as a cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devious' looks like the anagram signal but only gives its first letter; 'animated' shuffles FEUD, ME and D, L, R. 'Leporine' means hare-like.
explanation.definitionFit: The Looney Tunes character is a hapless hunter forever chasing Bugs Bunny with a shotgun.

clue.text: Wireless device turned on before interval

indicators.note: turned means the joined words are flipped round and read backwards
before places the word for on ahead of the word for interval

parts.note: re means on, concerning
a gap is an interval

explanation.surface: A radio set is switched on ahead of the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses REGAP. The surface reads 'turned on' as switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleeper is a small portable radio receiver that alerts its wearer to a message.

clue.text: See 2
See 7
Flagship boarded by king

indicators.note: boarded by means the next piece gets on board, inside the ship

parts.note: a steamer is a steamship
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: The leading vessel of a fleet has the monarch on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flagship' splits into Flag (the definition) and ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow pennant flown from a mast.

clue.text: Cold drink pumped with gas

indicators.note: pumped with means the next piece is forced inside

parts.note: rum is a drink
He is the chemical symbol for helium, a gas

explanation.surface: A beverage injected with carbonation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is the watery mucus from the nose or eyes that comes with a cold, and an old word for a cold itself.

clue.text: House in pain detailed on air

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the shortened pain follows the word for air

parts.note: wind is moving air

indicators.note: detailed means having the tail, the last letter, removed

parts.note: a sore is a painful spot

explanation.surface: A building where pain is set out on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' removes the last letter of SORE.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Windsor is the British royal family's dynasty, a house meaning a royal line.

clue.text: Means of communication, 28

definitions.meaning: the social media platform where short posts are sent
28 is CHEEP, and ... is also the chirping sound birds make

explanation.surface: A medium for messages, described by a bird's call.
explanation.definitionFit: The messaging platform is named after birdsong, and a chirp of a small bird is a twittering cheep.

clue.text: Pretty tiny wings for canary

parts.note: twee means sweet or pretty to a sickly degree

indicators.note: wings means the outside letters of the word, its two edges

explanation.surface: A rather small yellow songbird with pretty little wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweety Pie is the yellow cartoon bird of Looney Tunes, a canary forever escaping Sylvester.

clue.text: Aroma with allure picked up, imperial food

indicators.note: picked up means lifted upwards, so in a down clue the joined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: niff is British slang for a smell
it means sex appeal, allure

explanation.surface: A seductive scent catches the nose, and food of empire is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' sounds like a homophone signal but here reverses NIFFIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin is a light midday meal of British India, so food of the imperial Raj era.

clue.text: Part of clock checked when wound back, slow

indicators.note: wound back means the word is turned backwards, like a wound-back clock

parts.note: plaid is a checked tartan pattern
late means slow, behind time

explanation.surface: A clock's part was inspected after being turned back because it ran slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound back' reverses PLAID into DIALP.
explanation.definitionFit: The dial plate is the clock's face, the plate carrying the numerals.

clue.text: See 26
Noisome Casanova, footballer on page, keen to read up about it

indicators.note: about means wrapped round the other pieces
to read up in a down clue means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief, to weep

indicators.note: on in a down clue means placed above, so the footballer comes before the page

parts.note: Pele is the great Brazilian footballer

explanation.surface: A smelly ladies' man, a footballer on a page, eager to research the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to read up' reverses WEEP into PEEW, which goes 'about' PELE + P; 'it' refers back to that.
explanation.definitionFit: The Looney Tunes skunk is an amorous Frenchman who chases a cat, so a smelly would-be lover.

clue.text: Flower, not a sausage, for bird

parts.note: daffy is a dialect short form of daffodil
not a sausage is British slang for nothing at all, and duck is a score of nothing in cricket

explanation.surface: A flower, not a sausage, is offered in place of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a sausage' is a British phrase meaning nothing; in cricket a batsman out for no runs scores a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The lisping Looney Tunes character is a black duck, so a cartoon bird.

clue.text: Cosmic principle adopted by sovereign a year after uprising

indicators.note: after uprising says the hidden letters are read backwards
adopted by means taken into the following words, which hold the answer within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An idea of cosmic order taken up by a monarch a year after a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'adopted' in the definition; it is the hiding signal ('adopted by'), and 'after uprising' reverses GNAY.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chinese philosophy yang is the bright, active male force that balances yin in the universe.

clue.text: Sound from 22 down reasonable, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word for reasonable is spoken and spelt the other way

parts.note: cheap means reasonably priced

explanation.surface: Asking whether Tweety's noise is reasonable, by all accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 down is TWEETY, the cartoon canary.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheep is the short high chirp of a small bird such as a canary.

clue.text: 1, 6 and 10 shuffled for switchboard number

indicators.note: shuffled means the letters of the three number words are mixed together

parts.note: 1 is written as one
6 is written as six
10 is written as ten

explanation.surface: Three clue numbers mixed up to give a telephone line.
explanation.walkthrough: 1, 6 and 10 look like cross-references to other clues, but they are plain numbers spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension is one internal telephone line reached through an office switchboard.
